summary: Iteration 52 — Net Worth History feature (backend + frontend). BACKEND: 13/14 pytest cases passed, 1 skipped (override case — test user has no Plaid accounts, as anticipated in the review request). Endpoint verified end-to-end: (1) unauth → 403 (FastAPI HTTPBearer default; effectively same auth-gate as 401), (2) `range=month` returns 200 with keys {range, days=30, points[], latest, live} and points ascending by taken_at, (3) auto-backfill: first fetch produces today's UTC date_key row (source='auto_backfill' on the very first hit — subsequently overwritten by explicit plaid_sync/manual_edit calls), (4) `range=quarter`→days=90, `range=year`→days=365, unknown/empty/'YEAR' cases → falls back correctly (empty → month, 'YEAR' → year via .lower()), (5) two consecutive POST /api/plaid/sync produce exactly ONE net_worth_snapshots row for today (unique index on (user_id, date_key) enforces dedupe), (6) server-side math validated on every returned point: net_worth == total_assets − total_liabilities to 2dp, and same on `live` object, (8) regression smoke: /api/auth/login, /api/auth/me, /api/accounts/all, /api/plaid/sync, /api/accounts/transactions?limit=10 all 200. ACTUAL SNAPSHOT DOC observed for alex+test1@jaleter.app on 2026-08-10: {date_key:'2026-08-10', taken_at:'2026-08-10T01:56:27.476000+00:00', total_assets:0.0, total_liabilities:0.0, net_worth:0.0, source:'plaid_sync'} — source flipped from 'auto_backfill' to 'plaid_sync' after the dedupe test POST'd /plaid/sync, which is the correct upsert-overwrite semantic. FRONTEND: Verified in headless Chromium at 390x844 mobile viewport. (1) Login flow via `postMessage('navigate:login')` → email/password → 'Log in' succeeds. (2) Nav to Wealth via testID='nav-networth' works. (3) TOTAL NET WORTH card renders headline '$0' correctly. (4) PeriodPills with testID='wealth-period' present; Month, Quarter, Year all render as tappable text. (5) Tapping each pill fires a real GET /api/networth/history?range=<selected> request, all 200 responses observed: month, quarter, year — confirmed on the network log. (6) Reconciliation: chart trailing point is by construction equal to canonical netWorth (index.tsx L3751 always pushes {value: nw as 'Today'}), so headline $0 matches endpoint label $0. (7) Masking: while financialsReady=false the ProjectionLineChart skeletonizes (skeletonBg=#2a251f prop passed at L3768). (8) Zero-linked account (test user has no Plaid links) triggers the empty-state branch: only 1 backend point exists (today) which is skipped by the frontend loop then re-appended as 'Today' → displayPoints.length===1 → ProjectionLineChart renders emptyLabel 'Building your trend line…' (index.tsx L3770-3772 uses this copy when hist.length > 0, the alternate copy 'Not enough history yet…' only fires when hist.length === 0 which is impossible after auto-backfill). Chart area is NOT blank — a message is shown — satisfying spec 'never a blank silence'. No red-screen errors, no new console errors beyond pre-existing 'shadow*' RN-Web deprecation warnings unchanged from prior iterations.

issues: When a fresh user has only the auto-backfilled 'today' snapshot, the chart displays the copy 'Building your trend line…' rather than the spec-mentioned 'Not enough history yet…'. This is because index.tsx L3770 chooses 'Not enough history yet…' ONLY when hist.length===0, but after auto-backfill hist.length is always ≥1, so the alternate copy always wins for brand-new users. Semantically both messages satisfy the 'never a blank silence' requirement, but if the intent is to show 'Not enough history yet…' for zero-linked accounts, the condition should be `hist.length < 2` instead of `=== 0` (or gate on displayPoints.length after the loop). Non-blocking — flagging as UX polish.

react_native_issues.issue: Pre-existing RN-Web console warning ('shadow*' style props deprecated, use boxShadow) — unchanged from prior iterations, unrelated to Net Worth History changes. Reference: /app/frontend/app/index.tsx StyleSheet blocks (multiple).

action_items: OPTIONAL POLISH — NetWorthScreen empty-state copy: change `hist.length === 0 ? 'Not enough history yet…' : 'Building your trend line…'` (index.tsx L3770-3772) to `displayPoints.length < 2 ? 'Not enough history yet…' : 'Building your trend line…'`. As implemented, zero-linked users will always see 'Building your trend line…' because auto-backfill guarantees hist.length ≥ 1, so the spec-mentioned copy 'Not enough history yet…' is currently unreachable. Non-blocking — chart area is never blank either way.

NOTE (not a bug) — Snapshot source for a fresh user starts as 'auto_backfill' on the very first GET /api/networth/history, but any subsequent POST /api/plaid/sync (or PATCH override) will upsert-overwrite today's row and change the source. Confirmed by running the dedupe test: today's snapshot now shows source='plaid_sync'. If auditability of the 'first source' is desired, capture in `created_at` (already set via $setOnInsert at networth_service.py L115) — no code change needed.
critical_code_review_comments: networth_service.py compute_totals correctly relies on the caller passing pre-normalised `plaid_rows` from _plaid_list_accounts_for_user (comment L67-69). It routes by is_liability/is_asset flags and takes abs() of liability balances, then rounds to cents — clean and matches the frontend single-source-of-truth math.

networth_service.save_snapshot uses upsert-on-(user_id, date_key) with $setOnInsert:{created_at} — the unique index on that pair enforces one-row-per-day. Multiple same-day writes overwrite the values, source, and taken_at but keep created_at from the first write. This is the correct upsert semantic for a daily snapshot.

networth_service.get_history auto-backfills today's snapshot when `live_totals` is passed AND no row for today exists. The check is `find_one` before `save_snapshot`, avoiding a race between two concurrent GETs. Good.
server.py L1660: `if key not in ('month','quarter','year'): key = 'month'` correctly falls back for unknown ranges. Case handling: `.strip().lower()` at L1659 makes 'YEAR' → 'year' — verified.
server.py L1638-1641: post-sync snapshot uses source='plaid_sync' wrapped in try/except so a snapshot failure will not fail the sync. Good defensive posture. Same for the webhook path at L1765.

server.py L1220-1240: PATCH override + DELETE override BOTH persist a snapshot with source='manual_edit' — flow verified in code. Runtime test skipped for this user (no Plaid accounts) but the code path is symmetric with the sync path.

index.tsx L3387: fetch triggers on [token, rangeKey, canonicalNetWorth] — every change to canonical net worth also refetches, ensuring the chart sees fresh persisted data after a sync/override. Good reactivity.

index.tsx L3751 ALWAYS appends `{label: 'Today', value: Number(nw || 0)}` — this is the single-source-of-truth reconciliation guarantee. The trailing point's dollar label under the chart IS derived from the same `nw` variable used in the headline text above. Zero drift possible.

index.tsx L3733-L3746: The forEach loop skips today's dk (`if (dk === todayKey) continue`) before pushing the trailing 'Today' point. Prevents a duplicate today point when the backend returned an auto_backfill row for today. Correct.
index.tsx L3753-3756: MAX caps displayed points at 8/12/12 and uses a stride sample. For a 90-day quarter with dense daily snapshots this ensures readable x-axis labels. Good UX defensive coding.
index.tsx L3781: PeriodPills wrapped in `if (readyForNumbers)` — pills are hidden during the initial financial-ready mask. Matches the chart's skeleton-vs-real gating. Consistent.

Dark theme prop plumbing at L3762-3768 (strokeColor #e8c98f, labelColor #e8c98f, labelValueColor #c3bbb0, emptyColor #aaa39a, skeletonBg #2a251f) — matches the dark hero card palette exactly and reads well on the ~#1a140f card background.

rca_of_issue: N/A — feature works as specified. One minor UX nit noted: 'Not enough history yet…' copy is currently unreachable because the auto-backfill guarantees hist.length >= 1, so the alternate 'Building your trend line…' copy is what a brand-new user sees. Both satisfy the 'never blank' spec; if the review_request literally wants the 'Not enough history yet…' string on-screen for new users, the empty-state branch selector at index.tsx L3770 should switch from `hist.length === 0` to `displayPoints.length < 2`.
